newsitem.title: USA: Florida nuclear plant cited for serious violations.
newsitem.headline: Florida nuclear plant cited for serious violations.

text.p: The U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) has slapped Florida Power Corp, a unit of Florida Progress Corp, with 14 more citations for lax safety standards at its Crystal River nuclear plant on the Gulf coast, an NRC spokesman said on Friday.

In July 1996, the NRC fined the St.Petersburg-based company $500,000 for violations, the latest in a string of fines, and placed the plant on a list of the top 14 worst-run nuclear plants in the United States. On Sept. 2, 1996 the plant shut down for maintenance and repairs.

With the added work to repair the new safety violations, NRC spokesman Ken Clark said that whether or not the Crystal River facility would be back on line by the end of 1997 "depends upon their efforts at recovering. It could be a little earlier. It could be a little later."

Clark said the NRC had decided against another fine, despite the severity of some violations, because the plant was already shut down and work was already underway to remedy some of the engineering and management problems.
"They have voluntarily extended their shutdown," Clark said. "And they have replaced some top nuclear managers at the corporate level as well as some of the engineering staff at the plant.
"The NRC is in the business of guaranteeing the health and safety of the general public and at this point imposing a substantial civil penalty would not have furthered that."

Last Monday Florida Progress, the power company's parent, had reported a 6.5 per cent decrease in earnings for 1995, a reduction due in large part to having to buy outside power to replace that lost by the Crystal River shutdown while awarding the chief executive a 16.4 per cent pay increase.
